claim: For every finite-dimensional bipartite space \(B\otimes E\), orthogonal projection \(P\), integer \(n\ge6\), and degree parameter \(3\le D\le n/2\), let \(p_{n,D}\) be a polynomial of degree at most \(D\) with \(p_{n,D}(0)=1\) and \(|p_{n,D}(k)|\le\epsilon:=2^{-cD^2/n}\) for integers \(1\le k\le n\), where \(c>0\) is the universal constant in the established NOR-approximation lemma. Put \(P_i\) for the copy of \(P\) on pair \(B_iE_i\), \(q(x)=p_{n,D}(n-x)\), \(\widetilde P=q(\sum_{i=1}^n P_i)\), and \(\mu=\|P\|_\pi\), the projective tensor norm induced by local operator norms across \(B:E\). Then \(\widetilde P P^{\otimes n}=P^{\otimes n}\widetilde P=P^{\otimes n}\), \(\|\widetilde P-P^{\otimes n}\|_\infty\le\epsilon\), and \[\|\widetilde P\|_\pi\le\epsilon\sum_{s=0}^{D}\binom ns(2\mu)^s.\] In particular, with \(\kappa=\min\{(\dim B)^2,(\dim E)^2\}\), the known dimension bound \(\mu\le\kappa\) yields \(\|\widetilde P\|_\pi\le\epsilon(2\kappa)^D2^{n h(D/n)}\), improving the published bound for this same approximation by the factor \(\epsilon\), where \(h(t)=-t\log_2t-(1-t)\log_2(1-t)\).

correctness.rationale: For each integer \(s\le D<n\), the Newton finite difference samples only \(q(j)=p(n-j)\) with \(1\le n-j\le n\), hence \(|a_s|\le\epsilon 2^s\). The exact binomial identity for commuting projections and tensor-product submultiplicativity give the norm estimate. The joint spectrum proves the approximation error and the two identities on \(P^{\otimes n}\). No computation is being used as proof.

evidence: arXiv:2609.11771v1, Lemma 3, gives the baseline bound \(\Gamma\le (2\kappa)^D2^{n h(D/n)}\) using the complementary-projection expansion.
The same polynomial's error is \(\epsilon=2^{-cD^2/n}\), and the new bound is \(\epsilon\) times the corresponding binomial sum.

value.rationale: The bound is an exponential factor \(\epsilon\) smaller than the existing binomial-sum estimate for the same approximation. With \(D\) proportional to \(n\), it improves the norm penalty \(-2\log_2\Gamma\) in the one-shot blowing-up lemma by \(2cD^2/n\) bits. The gain is a concrete quantitative refinement of a step identified by the primary source as relevant to the strong-converse tradeoff; it does not claim a new capacity theorem.
